adopted.CLAUDE.md: adopted in full. This repo keeps no decision docs — docs/ holds plans and transient review artifacts only — and the source's § "Writing things down" routes a decision's alternatives to the PR or issue thread, which is what this repo already does. /audit-github-backlog carries the last upstream mention of decision docs, and it is declined. § "Language" is filled in rather than left as the source's adopter stub, and its § "Vetting" exit rule does not travel: that rule is about a stub over an unchecked stack, and this repo's vet.sh is real.

adopted..claude/skills/update-muthur/: this skill, under the name it has there — the source has renamed it three times (sync-upstream, sync-agent-infra, sync-muthur, update-muthur) and ships it as an unhydrated stub. The local copy keeps /sync-agent-infra and the hydrated procedure, so what lands from a commit touching this path is the procedure's own changes, never the stub framing or the name. Its watermark is source.json, not the source's watermark.json; nothing locates either by path, so neither rename travels.

adopted.scripts/vet.sh: rewritten for this stack: pnpm build alone and first (it regenerates .next/types/, which tsconfig includes), then styles:codegen alone, then the rest fanned out through run-parallel.sh. CLAUDE.md § Vetting carries the roster and why each check sits where it does. Read the source's edits for the idea; the file itself never lands.

declined..claude/skills/implement/: the source's redirect stub pointing /implement at /go, declined on the operator's call at the sync that renamed the skill: a permanent extra row is not worth keeping a retired name resolvable. `/plan` writes `/go <branch>` handoff blocks, and an older block saying `/implement` is a word an agent reads, not a skill they must load. Never — the stub only ever earns its place in the window right after the rename, and that window is closed
declined.ADOPTING.md: the source's guide for a repo taking the template on, which this repo did once and will not do again. Revisit only if a repo ever adopts from here — it would need its own, not a copy of the source's
declined.scripts/check-repo-identity.sh: never — it holds the source's own owner/repo to one home, the watermark's `repo` field, across the clone lines and gh recipes a human copies. The source's own vet.sh calls it the one line there that is that repo's alone: it keys on the catalog, which this repo declines, so it exits 0 here and would certify nothing
declined..claude/skills/update-muthur/catalog.md: never — the source's own inventory of what it ships, describing the source's tree rather than this repo. Step 4a reads it from the clone, where it is current by construction; a vendored copy would only drift, and the source's own banner says to delete it wherever it turns up downstream. check-skill-catalog.sh reads it at this path and skips its catalog assertions when absent, which is the normal state here; CLAUDE.md § "Adding or renaming a skill" records that. Lived at docs/catalog.md until the source moved it off a path an adopter can own
declined..claude/skills/spinoff/: seeds a sibling repo out of the project you are standing in, carrying its foundation rather than the source's. This repo's foundation is one personal site — there is no second product to fire out of it, and the source itself is the route to a new project. It also refuses on a catalog this repo declines, so adopting it means translating its sentinel. Declining it is why source.json carries no `lineage`: that field is written by /spinoff at the moment a repo is born, and this repo was hand-adopted, so the birth point is not recoverable from anything here. Revisit if a second repo is ever started from this one's layout rather than from the source
declined..claude/skills/detemplate/: turns a fresh "Use this template" fork into a project. This repo acquired its infrastructure by subset copy, not by forking the template, and is long past the one moment the skill exists for. Never
declined..claude/skills/propose-issue/: issues are opened by hand here, and the backlog is too small to dedupe against — revisit when filing becomes routine
declined..claude/skills/audit-github-backlog/: the backlog is a handful of issues an operator can read in one sitting — revisit when it is large enough that a sweep beats reading it
declined..claude/skills/release/: merging to main deploys automatically; there is no versioned release to cut
declined..claude/skills/hotfix/: no promotion path to bypass — main deploys straight to Pages
declined..claude/skills/log-review/: static site on GitHub Pages; there are no deployed logs to read
